pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: Extreme delta brush pattern on EEG coupled with a complex pelvic adnexal mass (mature ovarian teratoma). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: This is a severe autoimmune paraneoplastic syndrome. Ectopic neural tissue embedded within the ovarian teratoma expresses N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors, triggering the host immune system to generate IgG antibodies against the GluN1 subunit of extracellular NMDA receptors. These autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to NMDA receptors in the hippocampus and forebrain, causing antibody-mediated receptor cross-linking and internalization. The resulting depletion of synaptic NMDA receptors leads to severe disruption of dopaminergic and cholinergic pathways, manifesting sequentially as acute psychosis, movement disorders, autonomic instability, and hypoventilation. Definitively treated via prompt surgical resection of the teratoma alongside aggressive immunotherapy (plasma exchange, IVIG, and rituximab).
